transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee — what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, I guess what brought me in is... I've been having this issue with eating lately. After my evening class, I'll sometimes stop for food on the way home, and I just end up eating a massive amount. I'll get a full fast-food meal, grab candy from the vending machine, and then when I get back to the house, I just keep eating more snacks. It's like... I don't know, it's like I'm making up for the whole day all at once.
After one of these episodes of eating a large amount, do you ever do anything to try to compensate for it—like make yourself vomit, use laxatives, fast, or exercise excessively?

Yeah, I have. A few times, anyway. After those late-night eating spells, I've gone to the bathroom and made myself throw up. I just... I get scared that all that food is going to show on me, you know? Put on a bunch of weight. So, yeah, I've done that to try and get rid of it.
Over the past few months, about how often have these binge-eating and vomiting episodes been happening—would you say it's been at least once a week, and for how many months has this been going on?

I'd say it's been going on for about three months now. And yeah, it's usually at least one night a week. It almost always happens on a night after my evening class... I'll end up overeating like I described, and then make myself throw up afterward.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes of eating an objectively large amount of food with a sense of loss of control, occurring after evening classes, followed by self-induced vomiting to prevent weight gain. Episodes occur at least once weekly for the past 3 months, meeting frequency and duration criteria for Bulimia Nervosa. No indication of low body weight or restriction pattern suggestive of Anorexia Nervosa (which would exclude F50.2 in favor of the binge-purge subtype of AN), and behaviors are recurrent and compensatory, consistent with F50.2 rather than an unspecified feeding/eating disorder.
